# Parse precision/scale off a Tooling FieldDefinition DataType label, e.g.
# "Currency(16, 2)". Salesforce's two numbers are digits left/right of the decimal,
# so the DuckDB width is their sum (see _duckdb_type). The integer precision/scale
# columns on FieldDefinition are unreliable (0 for ~55% of numeric fields), so the
# label is the precision source.
context:
51: _CANONICAL_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$")
52: # The connector stamps timestamps at nanosecond precision; datetime parses six
53: # fractional digits, so clip the tail before parsing.
54: _NANOS_RE = re.compile(r"(\.\d{6})\d+")
55: # Parse precision/scale off a Tooling FieldDefinition DataType label, e.g.
56: # "Currency(16, 2)". Salesforce's two numbers are digits left/right of the decimal,
57: # so the DuckDB width is their sum (see _duckdb_type). The integer precision/scale
58: # columns on FieldDefinition are unreliable (0 for ~55% of numeric fields), so the
59: # label is the precision source.
60: _DATATYPE_PS_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:Currency|Number|Percent)\((\d+),\s*(\d+)\)$")
note: Must-pass. What-on-dense plus why: documents what the regex parses and why it parses the label string instead of the numeric columns (those columns are 0 for ~55% of numeric fields). A measured fact the regex cannot show.
